program_name: Bachelor in Social Work (IT: Laurea in Servizio sociale; DE: Bachelor in Sozialarbeit). Official MUR course code (CODICIONE): 0210106203900006. Faculty of Education, Free University of Bozen-Bolzano.
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The 'At a glance' box states: 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)' — note the order, which reflects the actual weighting: Italian and German dominate and ENGLISH IS THE SMALLEST of the three languages. Per-course language tags in the official 2026/27 course-offering listing ('Enrolled from 2025' study plan) give: YEAR 1 (60 CP) — Italian 24 CP (Principles of Sociology 6; Statistical and Demographic Analysis of Social Phenomena 6; Fundamentals of the Legal System and Fundamental Rights 6; General Psychology for Social Work 6), German 12 CP (Qualitative Methods and Methodologies in Social Research 6; Fundamentals in Social Work 6), English only 10 CP (Social Policy 5; Social Psychology 5), mixed IT/DE 6 CP (Social Pedagogy Throughout the Life Cycle), language-neutral 8 CP (Free Choice 4 + Orientation placement/internship 4). YEAR 2 (60 CP) — German 20 CP (Social Work Methodology and Organisation 10, all three sub-modules DE; History of Social Work 3; Sociology of the Family 5; LAB Observation of Parental Skills 2), English 14 CP (Inter- and Transnational Social Work 3; Family, Gender and Power 6; Psychology of Aging 5), Italian 12 CP (Developmental Psychology in Childhood and Adolescence 5; Family and Minors Law 5; LAB Digitalization and AI in Social Work 2), language-neutral 14 CP (Free Choice 4 + Professional internship 10). YEARS 1+2 COMBINED (120 CP): Italian 36 CP, German 32 CP, English 24 CP (20% of credits), mixed IT/DE 6 CP, language-neutral 22 CP. Year 3 (60 CP) teaching languages are NOT yet published, because the first cohort under this study plan (enrolled 2025) only reaches year 3 in 2027/28; year 3 does contain a 2 CP course 'Language Skills for Professional Communication'. There is NO English-only pathway and English is a minority language throughout: German is compulsory from semester 1 of year 1 and Italian carries the largest share of year 1. [uncertain] — the credit split is reconstructed from the per-module language tags on the unibz course-offering page for 2026/27; year 3 is unverified.
campus: Brixen-Bressanone (Faculty of Education campus, South Tyrol, ca. 40 km north-east of Bolzano). The 'At a glance' box states simply 'Campus: Brixen-Bressanone'. Faculty of Education Secretariat for this programme: Kreuzgasse 7 / via S. Croce 7, 39042 Brixen-Bressanone, tel. +39 0472 014000, faculty.education@unibz.it (the Faculty's other listed address is Regensburger Allee 16 / viale Ratisbona 16, same town). Critically, the ADMISSION INTERVIEW also takes place in Brixen-Bressanone in person — 'The interview will take place in Brixen-Bressanone' — with video conference possible only on written, motivated request submitted to the Faculty Secretariat at least 7 days before the interview date. Not Bozen-Bolzano, not NOI Techpark, not Bruneck-Brunico, not Trento, not Innsbruck.
degree_class: L-39 (Servizio sociale / Social Work / Sozialarbeit). 180 ECTS, 3 years, first-cycle degree. L-39 under DM 270/2004 is the successor of the old class 6 (Scienze del servizio sociale) under DM 509/1999 and is the qualification that gives access to Section B of the Italian professional register of social workers.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and STILL RECRUITING at the verification date. The programme page carries the explicit banner 'Courses will definetely be starting' (sic). Both the Early Bird and Late ranking lists for 2026/27 have been published (9 + 10 EU admitted). Because the 25-place EU quota was not filled, the Faculty opened the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: unibz's additional-application-session page lists 'Social Work' among the bachelor programmes accepting applications from 18/08/2026 to 04/09/2026 (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only). At the verification date of 2026-08-29 that window is OPEN and closes at noon on 04/09/2026 — six days later. Caveat stated on that page: applicants admitted through the additional session cannot attend the September intensive language courses, and beginners in the third language should already have A1 before enrolment.
is_new_programme: No — this is one of unibz's oldest degree programmes, not a new one. The Faculty of Education in Brixen-Bressanone has run a Social Work degree since 1999: a congress held on 21-22 November 2019 in Brixen was titled 'Aufbruch, Kontinuität und Wandel – 20 Jahre Studiengang Sozialarbeit an der Freien Universität Bozen' (Departure, Continuity and Change – 20 Years of the Social Work Degree Programme at the Free University of Bozen), attended by around 150 participants, which places the start of the programme in 1999 and makes 2026/27 roughly its 27th intake. What IS recent is the STUDY PLAN, restructured for the cohort enrolling in 2025/26: unibz maintains two separate course-offering pages, 'Course Offering – Enrolled from 2025' and 'Course Offering – enrolled before 2025', and the study plan described in this record is the 'from 2025' one, now in its second intake. [uncertain] — the 1999 founding year comes from press coverage of the 2019 anniversary congress, not from a unibz statement; the 2025 study-plan reform is inferred from the existence of the two parallel course-offering pages.
majors_tracks_study_plans: NO majors, NO tracks, NO alternative study plans, NO dual-study variant — a single 180 CP curriculum for all students, which distinguishes this programme from e.g. Design and Art or Food and Enogastronomy Sciences. Structure: YEAR 1 (60 CP) Principles of Sociology 6; Statistical and Demographic Analysis of Social Phenomena 6 (5 + 1 LAB); Qualitative Methods and Methodologies in Social Research 6; Fundamentals of Social Work and Social Policy 11 (Fundamentals in Social Work 6 + Social Policy 5); Fundamentals of the Legal System and Fundamental Rights 6; General Psychology for Social Work 6 (General Psychology 4 + LAB Life Skills 2); Social Pedagogy and Social Psychology 11 (Social Psychology 5 + Social Pedagogy Throughout the Life Cycle 6); Free Choice 4; Internship 4 (orientation placement). YEAR 2 (60 CP) Social Work Methodology and Organisation 10 (Methods and Techniques 3 + LAB 2 + Fields and Organisation of Social Work Practice 5); Social Work in Historical, Inter- and Transnational Contexts 6 (3 + 3); Parenthood and Family 11 (Sociology of the Family 5 + Family, Gender and Power 6); Life Cycle Psychology 12 (Developmental Psychology 5 + LAB Observation of Parental Skills 2 + Psychology of Aging 5); Family and Minors Law 5; LAB Digitalization and AI in Social Work 2; Free Choice 4; Internship 10. YEAR 3 (60 CP) Marginality, Social Change, Crime 9 (Criminal and Penitentiary Law 6 + Marginality and Social Change 3); Welfare, Territory and Sustainability 10 (Social Policies and Sustainability 5 + Planning and Evaluation of Social Policies and Services 3 + LAB Co-Programming and Co-Design 2); Community Work and Advocacy 6 (4 + LAB 2); Mental Health and Social Work 10 (Mental Health Promotion and Care 6 + Clinical and Intercultural Psychology 4); Strategies and Practices for Socio-Health Interventions 5 (3 + LAB 2); Language Skills for Professional Communication 2; Professionalizing Laboratory 1; Free Choice 4; Internship 10; Final Exam 3. SUPERVISED INTERNSHIP TOTALS 24 CP across the three years — the practice core of the degree. ATTENDANCE IS COMPULSORY: classes and seminars may be substituted partially by individual alternative activities agreed with the lecturer, WORKSHOP (LAB) attendance is compulsory with justified absences compensated by extra activities, and 'the total number of hours allotted to internships must be fully completed'. REGULATED PROFESSION: the degree leads to the Italian State Examination (esame di stato) for the profession of 'assistente sociale' and registration in Section B of the Albo degli Assistenti Sociali — a unibz graduate testimonial on the programme page states 'After passing the state exam and registering as a social worker, I started working as a social worker'. Part-time enrolment is available, chosen after enrolment in October, not at application.
english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY-CLOSED for a candidate who knows only English — this is one of the HARDEST unibz programmes for an English-only international applicant, harder than the trilingual Food and Enogastronomy Sciences bachelor. Three compounding barriers: (1) ENTRY GATE. Admission requires B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language, and failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank ('otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'). A candidate who can certify only English can certify only one language and is excluded outright. There is no B1 fallback: the admission-information document states 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams' at the unibz Language Centre — unlike Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, where B1 registrations are allowed and a B1 second language can be admitted where places remain. So the concrete minimum for a Turkish applicant is English B2 + Italian OR German B2. (2) IN-PERSON INTERVIEW. Selection turns on an admission interview held in Brixen-Bressanone; the candidate may choose to be interviewed in English, German or Italian, so the interview itself does not require Italian or German, but attendance in person in South Tyrol is the default and video conference requires a written motivated request at least 7 days in advance. (3) TEACHING REALITY. English carries only 10 of 60 CP in year 1 and 24 of 120 CP across years 1-2; Italian (36 CP) and German (32 CP) dominate, and a B1 level in the third language is required from the second semester of year 1 just to sit exams in that language. (4) GRADUATION AND PROFESSION. Exit levels are C1/C1/B2 — two languages at C1, stricter than the C1/B2/B2 of Food and Enogastronomy Sciences — and the degree's professional payoff (the Italian State Examination and registration in Section B of the Albo degli Assistenti Sociali) is in practice an Italian-language process. EMPIRICAL SIGNAL: no non-EU ranking list was published at all for 2026/27 in either session, and the 4 non-EU places went unused, while only 19 of 25 EU places were filled.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit-based ranking list built on an ADMISSION INTERVIEW plus a documentary assessment of prior work experience, preceded by an eliminatory language-eligibility gate (B2 in the 1st AND 2nd language). There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no portfolio and no school-grade scoring. A motivation cover letter (max 6,000 characters) is a compulsory upload. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. The Admission Committee is chaired by the Degree Course Director; for the 2026/27 Early Bird session it was Prof. Livia Taverna (chair) with Prof. Ulrike Loch and Prof. Doris Kofler, and Dr Elisabeth Berger as advisory member; for the Late session Prof. Livia Taverna (chair) with Prof. Doris Kofler and Prof. Urban Nothdurfter, and Dr Elisabeth Berger as advisory member.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school-leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (stated example: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after only one year is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research sets additional specific requirements for holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly; those applicants should contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). NO subject-specific prerequisites, NO minimum grade average and NO required school subjects are imposed — unlike Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (mathematics/science grades) or the economics bachelors (mathematics test). Language requirements (1st language B2, 2nd language B2) are a separate, eliminatory condition. No ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply (bachelor level). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed provided they do not belong to the same class and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents. Note for the professional pathway: the SSD codes now used in the curriculum are the post-2024-reform ones — GSPS-05/A and GSPS-06/A (sociology/social work, formerly SPS/07-SPS/08 area), PSIC-01/A, PSIC-02/A, PSIC-03/A (psychology, formerly M-PSI/01, M-PSI/04, M-PSI/05), PAED-01/A (pedagogy, formerly M-PED/01), GIUR-01/A and GIUR-05/A (law), STAT-03/B (demography/social statistics), INFO-01/A (computer science), SDEA-01/A (anthropology).
entry_exam_or_test: NONE in the sense of a written admission test — no unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test. The selective instrument is an ADMISSION INTERVIEW (see 'interview'). The only formal EXAMINATIONS connected with admission are LANGUAGE exams at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who choose that route of proof: Early Bird session — online, 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late session — online, 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). No Language Centre exam session is listed for the Additional Application Session, so an applicant in that window must already hold accepted proof. IMPORTANT RESTRICTION: for this programme 'you can only register for B2 level exams' — there is no B1 option, because both the 1st and the 2nd language must be at B2. Only one level per language per session. Separately, AFTER admission there is a non-selective THIRD-LANGUAGE PLACEMENT TEST for admitted students who cannot certify their third language; the date is communicated by e-mail.
selection_scoring: The admission procedure is based on three criteria: (1) a cover letter of maximum 6,000 characters on the motivation for choosing the study programme; (2) an admission interview assessing knowledge and understanding of current social issues and communication skills — MAXIMUM 80 POINTS IN TOTAL; (3) any experience the applicant has had working in the field of social work — MAXIMUM 20 POINTS. The published scale therefore totals 100 points, of which 80 % is the interview and 20 % prior social-work work experience. Tie-break: in the event of equal scores, priority goes to the YOUNGER applicant. NO minimum passing score is published — unlike Design (42/100), Critical Creative Practices (60/100), EMMA (55/95) or Entrepreneurship (70/100) — and no school-grade component, no grade-average requirement and no OFA-triggering thresholds exist. The Admission Committee 'will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline'. COMPETITION SIGNAL for 2026/27: demand was well below capacity. Early Bird admitted 9 EU/equivalent against 20 EU places and published NO non-EU list at all (0 of 4 non-EU places used); Late admitted 10 EU against 5 Late places plus 11 Early Bird carry-over places; cumulative EU admissions 19 against the 25-place EU quota, which is why the Additional Application Session was opened. The binding constraints are therefore the B2/B2 language gate, the in-person interview and the deadlines — not the score. [uncertain] — the cover letter is listed as criterion 1 but is assigned no point value in any published document, so it is unclear whether it is scored inside the 80-point interview assessment or used only as an eligibility/qualitative document; and unlike most unibz programmes, the Social Work ranking lists publish only Applicant IDs and rank positions with NO scores, so no empirical cut-off can be derived.
bonus_points: NONE. There is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation) and no extracurricular-activity bonus (Bachelor in Computer Science). The only credit for anything beyond the interview is criterion 3 of the ordinary rubric — up to 20 points for prior experience working in the field of social work, which is part of the 100-point scale rather than a bonus on top of it. The only other preference mechanism is the age tie-break in favour of the younger candidate. Note that the 20 experience points are a genuine structural advantage for mature applicants and career-changers, and there is no published definition of what counts as 'experience in the field of social work' (paid employment, internship, civil service, volunteering) or how it is documented, since the portal upload list mentions only the cover letter.
portfolio_and_materials: NO portfolio, NO video, NO project proposal, NO reference letters and NO CV are formally required — the only substantive material is the MOTIVATION COVER LETTER, capped at 6,000 CHARACTERS, on the motivation for choosing the study programme. The admission-information document's portal instruction list contains exactly one item: 'In the application portal, you shall: upload the cover letter'. No file format or file-size limit is published for it (contrast the 20 MB PDF portfolio cap and 2-page project proposal of the design/creative programmes). No language is prescribed for the cover letter; since the interview may be held in English, German or Italian and documentation for unibz applications is generally accepted in any of the three teaching languages, the letter is presumably acceptable in any of the three. Candidates must upload the required documents by the application deadline; once submitted, the application cannot be modified, and 'filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration'. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. [uncertain] — the permitted language(s) and file format of the cover letter, and the documentary evidence required to claim the 20 work-experience points, are not specified in any published unibz document for this programme.
interview: YES — the admission interview is the CENTRAL selection instrument for this programme and carries up to 80 of the 100 points. Published dates for 2026/27, one per application session: EARLY BIRD — 19/05/2026; LATE APPLICATION — 21/07/2026; ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION — 11/09/2026. Purpose: 'to asses knowledge and understanding of current social issues and communication skills'. LOCATION: the interview takes place IN PERSON in Brixen-Bressanone; the exact location and time are published on the study programme website. LANGUAGE: 'You can choose whether to attend the admission colloquium in English, German or Italian' — a decisive concession for international applicants, because it means the selection conversation itself need not be in Italian or German even though the degree is Italian/German-dominant. REMOTE OPTION: 'If you are unable to attend the interview appointment due to serious logistical difficulties, it is possible to hold the interview in a video conference. You must provide a written and motivated request to the Faculty Secretariat at least 7 days before the date of the interview' — for an applicant based in Türkiye this 7-day written-request route is the practical path, and it is discretionary rather than automatic. Faculty Secretariat contact for that request: faculty.education@unibz.it, +39 0472 014000.
conditional_admission: Applicants still in their final year of upper secondary school may apply — selection is by interview and work experience, not by school grades, so applying before graduation is the normal case rather than a special regime. The diploma is uploaded at enrolment: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' Holders of a foreign qualification are ADMITTED WITH RESERVE until the recognition documents (diploma, translation, ARDI/CIMEA statements) are uploaded — the ranking decree states 'Fino a quando non avrai caricato la documentazione sopra indicata, potrai essere ammesso/ammessa solo con riserva' (until you have uploaded the documentation indicated above, you can only be admitted with reserve); if the qualification is judged suitable the reserve is lifted, otherwise the applicant is excluded. unibz 'performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents', and an applicant who turns out not to possess a valid admission qualification 'can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are non-refundable EXCEPT if the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam (maturità/Matura) or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. NOTE: the ≥120/140 ECTS conditional-admission thresholds and the 11/12/2026 late-enrolment window described in the field schema are MASTER-level rules and do not apply to this bachelor programme.
ofa_rules: NONE. No OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) exists for this programme: the admission-information document and the programme page contain no OFA section, no mathematics or chemistry test, and no grade thresholds that would trigger additional learning requirements. This contrasts with Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics and Tourism Sport and Event Management (test-based OFA in mathematics) and with Food and Enogastronomy Sciences and Computer Science (grade-based OFA). The functional equivalent of an additional obligation here is purely linguistic: an admitted student who cannot certify the third language must sit a placement test and follow an assigned learning path, and needs B1 in the third language from the second semester of year 1 in order to take curricular examinations held in that language.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language rule is ELIMINATORY: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' ENTRY: 1st language B2, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required. FROM THE 2ND SEMESTER OF YEAR 1: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that language. EXIT (to graduate): 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 — the standard, stricter unibz trilingual exit profile, one step harder in the second language than Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (C1/B2/B2). Language positions are defined by the applicant's own proficiency, not by which language it is: the 1st language is the one in which the applicant is strongest (B2 or C1), the 3rd the weakest, possibly absolute beginner. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. Because both admission levels are B2, applicants may register at the unibz Language Centre for B2 EXAMS ONLY — there is no B1 exam route for this programme. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language take a placement test (details by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path aiming at B2 'as soon as possible'. Language Centre courses are FREE: extensive courses 4 h/week during semesters, intensive courses 8 h/week between semesters, and a three-week pre-semester intensive session 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day). A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that September pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there — a trap for anyone admitted through the Additional Application Session, whose ranking list is only published by 18/09/2026, after the intensive courses have finished. Target levels in the third language: B1 by the end of year 1, B2 by the end of year 2. Documentary note: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required. This 'B2/B2/none' pattern is the standard mid-tier unibz trilingual entry profile: the same as Bachelor in Computer Science, harder than Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (B2/B1/none, with B2 merely preferred in the 2nd language) and easier than Public Policy and Innovative Governance or Accounting and Finance (C1/B2/none). Position is set by the candidate's own strength ranking, not by which language it is, so any two of German, Italian and English at B2 satisfy the rule. The direct operational consequence of the B2/B2 profile is that the unibz Language Centre only accepts registrations for B2-level exams for this programme ('Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams'), with one level per language per session — there is no possibility of demonstrating a B1 second language and being admitted on remaining places, which IS possible for Food and Enogastronomy Sciences. A third distinguishing feature: from the second semester of year 1 a B1 in the third language becomes a hard prerequisite for sitting exams delivered in that language, and because the curriculum spreads compulsory credits across all three languages in both year 1 and year 2, that threshold binds in practice rather than in theory.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is the full standard unibz trilingual exit profile and a substantial gate: a student admitted at B2/B2/none must raise BOTH the first and second languages from B2 to C1 and go from zero (or A1) to B2 in the third language within three years, while also completing 24 CP of supervised internship. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support the third-language part of this (B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2), with A1 beginner courses available only in the September pre-semester intensive session. Compared with Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (C1/B2/B2 exit), this programme demands one CEFR step more in the second language.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is required FROM THE 2ND SEMESTER OF THE FIRST YEAR as the minimum level for taking the curricular examinations held in that specific language. This is a binding rather than nominal constraint for this programme, because compulsory credits are spread across all three languages from the start: in year 1 alone the compulsory load is Italian 24 CP, German 12 CP, English 10 CP plus a 6 CP mixed IT/DE module, and in year 2 it is German 20 CP, English 14 CP, Italian 12 CP. A student whose third language is Italian would be blocked from roughly 24 CP of year-1 exams without B1; a student whose third language is German would be blocked from 12 CP in year 1 and 20 CP in year 2. There is no programme-specific mid-January deadline of the kind imposed by the Bachelor in Computer Science. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test and are assigned a learning path targeting B1 by end of year 1 and B2 by end of year 2.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways: (1) the main teaching language of the final high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter or document issued by the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if it is not on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application — ONLINE exams for 2026/27: Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); B2 LEVEL ONLY for this programme, one level per language per session; if an application is started outside a registration period the applicant must return to the portal during one of the listed periods. Additional route for foreign and bi-/multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2ND AND/OR 3RD LANGUAGE (not the 1st), subject to Language Centre approval; the school-leaving certificate is uploaded under the respective language in the 'upload language certificates' section. Administrative detail: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma. Exam structure, duration, administration and typical result-processing times are published on the Language Centre 'study in three languages' page.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'), a trilingual DE/IT/EN document applying university-wide. Rules: (1) the certificate must assess ALL FOUR skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must show adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the exam was passed' — the LOWEST sub-skill governs; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION for failed exam parts and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides them; (5) certificates obtained through an online 'home edition' exam are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged with an asterisk in the list; (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers, lectors or teachers are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised. VALIDITY: international language certificates must not be older than FIVE YEARS before the date of submission, with the entire calendar year counting from 1 January; items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September if places remain — and it WAS opened for this programme in 2026/27): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. Each session has its own admission interview date (19/05/2026, 21/07/2026, 11/09/2026 respectively), so the deadline is effectively a two-stage commitment: submit by the application deadline, then be available for the interview in Brixen-Bressanone about three weeks later. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in one session may apply again in the next — Applicant ID 151665 appears in BOTH the Early Bird list (rank 9) and the Late list (rank 8) for 2026/27, evidence that re-application across sessions happens in practice. At the verification date of 2026-08-29 the Additional Application Session is OPEN and closes at noon on 2026-09-04.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 4-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) for the study visa. For academic year 2026/27 this window is closed; the next opportunity for a non-EU applicant living abroad is the 2027/28 Early Bird session (expected around March-April 2027). Practical note for Turkish applicants: the non-EU route also collides with the interview logistics, since the Early Bird interview date (19/05/2026) falls three weeks after the application deadline and requires either travel to Brixen-Bressanone or an approved video-conference request filed at least 7 days in advance.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish applicants: (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of Legislative Decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a visa for tourism is NOT sufficient. Critical warning, repeated in both the admission-information document and the signed ranking decrees: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin' — losing access to the Late and Additional sessions, to the 25-place EU quota, and being pushed onto the 4-place non-EU list. For this programme in 2026/27 that distinction was decisive in an unusually stark way: the parity route led to two further sessions (Late, and the Additional session still open on the verification date), whereas the non-EU-abroad route closed on 28/04/2026 and produced no published non-EU ranking list at all.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27, confirmed identically by the admission-information document, the brochure and the programme page. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: EARLY BIRD APPLICATION 20 places, LATE APPLICATION 5 places — summarised in the 'At a glance' box as 'Places available: 25 EU + 4 non-EU'. Non-EU citizens living abroad: EARLY BIRD APPLICATION 4 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule (EU/equivalent only): 'any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application'. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE — the programme is substantially undersubscribed: Early Bird admitted 9 EU/equivalent against 20 places, and the Early Bird decree contains NO non-EU ranking section at all, meaning 0 of the 4 non-EU places were awarded; Late admitted 10 EU/equivalent against 5 Late places plus 11 Early Bird carry-over places (16 available). Cumulative EU/equivalent admissions 19 against the 25-place EU quota, leaving roughly 6 EU places for the Additional Application Session. This makes Social Work one of the least competitive unibz bachelor programmes by raw numbers — the scarce resource is language-eligible, interview-available applicants rather than places. Corroborating scale data from the MUR/AlmaLaurea transparency page for this course (CODICIONE 0210106203900006): 9 graduates in 2025 and 13 graduates in 2024.

required_documents: At application (online via https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; the completed online form; THE COVER LETTER (max 6,000 characters) on the motivation for choosing the programme, which is the only item explicitly listed as a portal upload under the admission procedure; language certificates uploaded under 'upload language certificates' (MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd) and/or registration for Language Centre B2 exams under 'enrol for language exams'; the diploma of the qualification if already obtained abroad (otherwise uploaded at enrolment); for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay (plus renewal request if expired). NOTE: there is NO 'study career' Excel template for this programme — that structured upload is a master-level requirement; and there are no school report cards or grade tables to upload, because school grades are not scored. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload: the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Once submitted the application cannot be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the beginning of the academic year; non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit once obtained, in person or by e-mail. application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly NON-REFUNDABLE: 'Application fee: € 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons) pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year in two instalments: 1st instalment €600 (including the €16 revenue stamp / marca da bollo) — this is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, due by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees and the programme's own admission-information PDF: https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-social-work_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: NO programme-specific scholarship exists for this degree — unlike Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, which has the dedicated Meran-Merano municipal award. The only routes are the general unibz/provincial ones. MAIN ROUTE: the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for Higher Education Support (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario) in three annual categories — ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants fostering postgraduate studies. Applications for ordinary and merit study grants are filled in and sent through the provincial e-government service online, with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association (sh.asus). Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid for the academic year. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively ineligible in year one. Other listed sources: Italian government grants (which also exempt the holder from tuition fees), Austrian and German (BAföG) grants, DAAD summer-course scholarships, and loans from Italian banks. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. Until that documentation is uploaded the applicant is admitted only 'with reserve'; unibz performs its own checks and reserves the right to request additional documents, and a candidate found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Recognition of credit points from previous UNIVERSITY studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses; the application is filed at the Faculty Secretariat and, per the 2026/27 ranking decrees, submitted online via the unibz Intranet by 18/09/2026. The Faculty organises appointments for the preliminary evaluation of previous university careers (in Italian and in German). SEPARATE, POST-GRADUATION RECOGNITION ISSUE: for social work the degree alone does not confer the right to practise — see the State Examination note under programme_specific_dates — and holders of a social-work qualification obtained outside the EU must go through a distinct professional-title recognition procedure via the Italian Ministry of Justice before they can register in the Albo.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only, 02/03-28/04/2026 (€50 non-refundable fee) → be available for the admission interview on 19/05/2026 in Brixen-Bressanone, or request a video conference in writing at least 7 days beforehand → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (4 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). The Universitaly application is MANDATORY — 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and the ranking decree is blunter still: 'La mancata preiscrizione su Universitaly comporta la nullità della domanda di preiscrizione e di immatricolazione presentata all'università' (failure to pre-enrol on Universitaly voids the application and enrolment submitted to the university). Only ONE study programme may be selected on Universitaly. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa; unibz warns that admission does not guarantee a visa or even an appointment at the Italian consular representation, and that holding a study visa confers no automatic right to complete enrolment. FINANCIAL MEANS for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs, excluding tuition fees; total proof of at least €36,000 for a bachelor programme (€24,000 for a master); health insurance and visa expenses on top. AFTER ARRIVAL: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 WORKING DAYS of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund. Verified 2026-08-29. TIME-CRITICAL: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 are closed and their ranking lists are published, but the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (18/08-04/09/2026, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only) is OPEN at the verification date and closes at noon on 04/09/2026 — six days later — with the admission interview on 11/09/2026 in Brixen-Bressanone. (1) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING is reconstructed from the per-course language tags on the unibz course-offering page for 2026/27 ('Enrolled from 2025' plan) cross-referenced with the brochure study plan; it covers YEARS 1 AND 2 ONLY. Year 3 language tags are not published because the first cohort under this plan reaches year 3 in 2027/28, so the whole-degree English share cannot be stated. Free-choice credits (4 CP per year) and internships (24 CP total) carry no fixed language and are excluded from the per-language totals. (2) SCORING GAPS: the cover letter is criterion 1 of the admission procedure but carries no published point value, so it is unclear whether it is scored within the 80-point interview assessment or serves only as a qualitative/eligibility document; no minimum passing score is published; and no documentary standard is given for the up-to-20-point prior work experience. (3) NO SCORES IN THE RANKING LISTS: unusually for unibz, both 2026/27 decrees publish only rank positions and Applicant IDs, with no scores and no list of applicants excluded on language grounds.
